ent_concept_human_robot_collaboration_sa.name: Human-Robot Collaboration Safety
ent_concept_human_robot_collaboration_sa.summary: The set of standards, sensors, control laws, and workplace designs that ensure safe coexistence and cooperation between humans and robots.
ent_concept_human_robot_collaboration_sa.body:
## Overview

Human-Robot Collaboration Safety is the collection of standards, sensors, control laws, and workspace design that ensures safe coexistence and collaboration between humans and robots in shared workspaces. It encompasses core standards such as ISO 13482, ISO/TS 15066, IEC 61508, ISO 13849, and IEC 62368, as well as regional market access requirements including CE, UL, FCC, CR, and CCC. What it truly changes is not a single safety device, but the entire legal foundation that takes a robot from laboratory prototype to commercial deployment.

ent_concept_world_model.name: World Model
ent_concept_world_model.summary: A learned or hand-crafted internal model that predicts future states of the environment, enabling planning and reasoning in robotics and AI.
ent_concept_world_model.body:
## Overview

A World Model is a learned predictive model of "how the environment will evolve given the current state and action." It enables robots to reason about action consequences, evaluate candidate plans, and generate synthetic training data through "imagination," without needing to interact with the real environment each time. In contrast to VLA policies (which learn "see what, do what"), world models learn "what happens if I do this," and are becoming key infrastructure connecting simulation and reality, perception and decision-making (Source: Project Wiki Chapter 20).
